description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several large language model variants, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed “SepLLM” and “StrmLLM” methods, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000, and uses a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick marks at 0.1 intervals, also on a linear scale. Six distinct lines are plotted: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line) starts near 3.35 and steadily declines to approximately 2.5; “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid) begins near 3.35 and drops to about 2.62; “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid) starts near 3.3 and converges to ~2.55; “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid) begins near 3.25 and ends at ~2.53; “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid) starts near 3.2 and converges to ~2.52; and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid) begins near 3.3 and ends at ~2.51. All lines exhibit a steep initial decline in loss followed by a slower convergence toward their final values, with “SepLLM (n=128)” achieving the lowest final loss and “Vanilla” the highest among the group.
